findings.title: Changing the recreate result exit code breaks the documented automation contract
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` was previously 4 and is changed to 3 so that 4 can be reused for the disabled-feature case. The update-compatibility guide explicitly instructs automation consumers to rely on the `check` command's exit code to choose between rolling and recreate updates. Existing pipelines that treat 4 as the recreate-required result will now see 3 as an unexpected failure and may not perform the required recreate upgrade. Preserve the existing recreate code and allocate a new unused code for feature-disabled (or make this an explicitly versioned breaking API change with a migration path).

findings.title: The newly documented exit-code behavior is not asserted
findings.body: The disabled-feature test verifies only stderr text and never checks that the command exits with code 4. Likewise, the incompatible-version cases only check their messages and do not assert the newly changed recreate-required code 3. Since these numeric codes are documented as the scriptable interface, a regression that returns 0, a generic error code, or swaps the two codes would pass this test suite. Assert `CLIResult.exitCode()` for disabled and incompatible `check` invocations.
